Prerequisites: Differential and integral calculus, matrices and differential equations, complex variables and transform techniques, signals and systems.
CourseOutcomes: CO1: Understand the characteristics of signals and systems in time domain and frequency domain.
CO2: Understand the transforms and their properties (DTFT, Z-Transform, DFT, FFT).
CO3: Analyze discrete-time LTI systems in Fourier and Z domains.
CO4: Synthesize FIR and IIR digital filter structures (Direct, Cascade, Parallel, Lattice).
CO5: Design FIR and IIR type digital filters for signal processing, equalization, and noise cancellation.
UnitTitles: Unit I: Basic Elements of Digital Signal Processing
UnitTexts: Review of signals & systems, DTFT, Z transform, DFT, DFT properties, ROC, and system function analysis.

Efficient computation of DFT, FFT algorithms: radix-2 and radix-4 FFT algorithms, decimation in time and decimation in frequency algorithms, use of FFT algorithms in linear filtering (overlap-add, overlap-save), reconstruction and aliasing in time and frequency domains.

FIR and IIR filters - direct form realization, cascade form, and linear phase realization. IIR filter - direct form I, direct form II, cascade form, parallel form, Lattice and lattice-ladder form realization, finite wordlength effects.

Linear phase FIR filter, characteristic response, location of zeros, design of FIR filter - windowing (Rectangular, Bartlett, Hann, Hamming, Blackman, Kaiser), frequency sampling method, moving average filters. Design of IIR filters from analog filters - Butterworth & Chebyshev prototypes, Impulse invariance, bilinear transformation, matched z-transform. Channel equalization, adaptive noise cancellation, and LMS adaptive FIR filter.
